title: ⚡ Dad Complains About Electric Bill, So I Built Him an Energy Dashboard and Found the Panels Lied ⚡
why_read: A relatable and well-constructed personal data project combining solar monitoring, utility bill data, and smart home device tracking into one dashboard with real anomaly detection.
analysis: The author built a home energy dashboard that pulls live per-panel solar production data, flags underperforming or dead microinverters, compares actual output against a government solar production model, and merges this with utility bill and smart-plug data. This is a good practical example of integrating multiple real-world APIs and data sources into a single diagnostic tool, which has broader relevance to anyone building home automation or monitoring dashboards. It's a personal project rather than a generalizable technique, but the engineering of pulling together disparate data sources is genuinely useful to see.
